description: SkillEvaluator dataset for the Triton ONNX Model Repository skill. 34 positive and 12 negative cases, one per unique feature or failure mode. Verified against Triton 26.10 on an A100 host.

cases.prompt: I have an ONNX file with fixed input shape [4]. Set it up to serve on Triton locally.
expected_behavior: Inspect the ONNX graph to confirm no dynamic axis
Build <repo>/<model>/1/model.onnx
Start tritonserver without config.pbtxt (auto-complete)
Confirm /v2/repository/index shows state READY
Return the Output Contract including server command and a Python client snippet
cases.ground_truth: Auto-complete sets max_batch_size: 0, backend: onnxruntime, dims matching the graph. No config.pbtxt file written.

cases.prompt: My ONNX model has a dynamic batch dimension. Serve it with Triton and let batching happen automatically.
expected_behavior: Read the graph and confirm leading axis is dynamic
Skip config.pbtxt
Start the server with defaults
Verify /v2/models/<model>/config shows max_batch_size: 4 and dynamic_batching enabled
cases.ground_truth: Auto-complete sets max_batch_size: 4 (server default) and attaches a dynamic_batching block with preferred_batch_size [4].

cases.prompt: Write me a config.pbtxt for a FP32 add model with two inputs of shape [4] using the modern backend syntax.
expected_behavior: Produce a config.pbtxt using `backend: "onnxruntime"`
Include input and output sections with TYPE_FP32 dims [4]
Include instance_group KIND_CPU
Set max_batch_size: 0
cases.ground_truth: The config uses `backend: "onnxruntime"` (not `platform:`) and the `TYPE_FP32` spelling.

cases.prompt: My existing config.pbtxt uses `platform: "onnxruntime_onnx"`. Does that still work on Triton 26.10, or do I need to migrate?
expected_behavior: Confirm `platform: "onnxruntime_onnx"` still loads
Point at docs/examples/model_repository/simple/config.pbtxt as the in-tree example
Recommend `backend: "onnxruntime"` for new configs
cases.ground_truth: Both forms load READY and serve correctly. The modern form is `backend: "onnxruntime"`.

cases.prompt: I want max_batch_size 16 with a preferred batch size of 8 and 100ms queue delay. Write the config.
expected_behavior: Write max_batch_size: 16
Add a dynamic_batching { preferred_batch_size: [8] max_queue_delay_microseconds: 100000 } block
Warn that hand-written mbs>0 does NOT implicitly enable the batcher without the block
cases.ground_truth: A hand-written config needs an explicit dynamic_batching block. Auto-complete adds it; a hand-written config does not.

cases.prompt: Run my ONNX model on GPUs 0 and 1 with 2 instances each.
expected_behavior: Write instance_group [{ count: 2, kind: KIND_GPU, gpus: [0, 1] }]
Add --gpus all to the docker run command
Point at nv_gpu_utilization and nv_gpu_memory_used_bytes metrics
cases.ground_truth: instance_group with KIND_GPU and explicit gpus list. Container needs --gpus all.

cases.prompt: I don't have a GPU. Set up Triton ONNX inference on CPU.
expected_behavior: Write instance_group [{ kind: KIND_CPU }] or omit instance_group
Drop --gpus all from docker run
Confirm auto-complete still works
cases.ground_truth: KIND_CPU places on CPU; docker run without --gpus still works.

cases.prompt: I have versions 1, 2, and 3 of my ONNX model in the repository. Which one does Triton serve by default?
expected_behavior: Explain default version policy serves the highest numeric version
Confirm version 3 is served
Mention `/v2/models/<model>` reports the versions array
cases.ground_truth: Default policy serves version 3. Verified against a repo with 1/, 2/, and 3/.

cases.prompt: Serve version 1 and version 3 at the same time for A/B comparison, skip version 2.
expected_behavior: Add version_policy: { specific: { versions: [1, 3] } } to config.pbtxt
Show client code using model_version="1" and model_version="3"
Note that a request for version 2 returns 404 'version 2 is not found'
cases.ground_truth: `version_policy: { specific: { versions: [1, 3] } }` loads both; v2 requests return HTTP 404.

cases.prompt: I want all versions of my model to be callable by clients.
expected_behavior: Add version_policy: { all: {} } to config.pbtxt
Explain each version appears as its own entry in /v2/repository/index
cases.ground_truth: `version_policy: { all: {} }` loads every numeric version directory present.

cases.prompt: I don't want to rename resnet.onnx to model.onnx. Can I keep the original name?
expected_behavior: Add default_model_filename: "resnet.onnx" to config.pbtxt
Leave the file named resnet.onnx in the version directory
Confirm load as READY
cases.ground_truth: `default_model_filename: "resnet.onnx"` overrides the default model.onnx name; the file loads as READY.

cases.prompt: My ONNX file was converted from TensorFlow. The input is named 'image:0' and the output is 'resnet50/predictions/Softmax:0'. How do I handle those names in the config?
expected_behavior: Quote the names exactly in config.pbtxt: `name: "image:0"` and `name: "resnet50/predictions/Softmax:0"`
Use the same literal names on the client side
Warn that mismatches produce `unexpected inference input` errors
cases.ground_truth: Names with `:0` and `/` are valid when quoted. The client passes the exact string to InferInput and as_numpy.

cases.prompt: I have a 5-class classifier. I want the client to get class names back, not raw logits.
expected_behavior: Add `label_filename: "labels.txt"` to the output section
Place labels.txt next to config.pbtxt, one label per line
Show client using InferRequestedOutput with class_count=3
Explain return format `b'<probability>:<class_id>:<label>'`
cases.ground_truth: Top-K classes returned as byte strings of the form `<prob>:<class_id>:<label>`.

cases.prompt: I have an ONNX text-echo model that takes strings in and out. How do I declare it in config.pbtxt and call it from Python?
expected_behavior: Use data_type: TYPE_STRING in config.pbtxt
On the client use InferInput with datatype "BYTES" and np.array([...], dtype=object)
Note the output comes back as Python bytes; decode with .decode('utf-8')
cases.ground_truth: TYPE_STRING in config maps to "BYTES" on client. Output is numpy array of bytes objects.

cases.prompt: Enable response caching for my deterministic ONNX model so repeat requests don't re-run the backend.
expected_behavior: Start the server with `--cache-config local,size=1048576`
Add `response_cache { enable: true }` to config.pbtxt
Warn that without the server flag, the model-level flag is a no-op
Point at nv_cache_num_hits_per_model, nv_cache_num_misses_per_model, nv_cache_num_lookups_per_model
cases.ground_truth: Both the server --cache-config flag AND the model config response_cache block are required. Verified: 3 identical + 1 different → 2 hits / 2 misses.

cases.prompt: Make my ONNX model run warmup inferences at load time so the first real request isn't slow.
expected_behavior: Add a model_warmup block with batch_size: 1 and zero_data: true for each input
Explain the model won't reach READY until warmup completes
Note Triton does not log explicit 'warming up' lines
cases.ground_truth: `model_warmup` block with `zero_data: true` delays READY until warmup finishes; failed warmup fails the load.

cases.prompt: My ONNX model has weights stored in a separate weights.bin file alongside model.onnx. Will Triton load that?
expected_behavior: Confirm Triton loads both files from the version directory
Explain model.onnx references the sidecar by name
No special config.pbtxt entries needed
Warn that a missing weights file surfaces as an ONNX Runtime load error
cases.ground_truth: Triton loads `model.onnx` + `weights.bin` side by side without extra configuration.

cases.prompt: I want auto-complete to use max_batch_size 16 instead of 4 by default for all my ONNX models.
expected_behavior: Add `--backend-config=default-max-batch-size=16` to the tritonserver command
Explain this only affects batchable graphs (dynamic leading axis)
Note fixed-shape graphs still get max_batch_size: 0
cases.ground_truth: `--backend-config=default-max-batch-size=16` changes auto-complete's default for batchable graphs. Fixed-shape graphs unaffected.

cases.prompt: I have an empty config.pbtxt file in my model directory. Does Triton treat it as a missing config?
expected_behavior: Explain an empty config.pbtxt is equivalent to no config.pbtxt
Auto-complete runs normally
Model loads READY with the auto-generated configuration
cases.ground_truth: Empty `config.pbtxt` loads READY via auto-complete; equivalent to omitting the file.

cases.prompt: Run Triton with on-demand model loading via the API, not loading everything at startup.
expected_behavior: Start tritonserver with `--model-control-mode=explicit`
Use `POST /v2/repository/models/<model>/load` to load a model
Use `POST /v2/repository/models/<model>/unload` to unload
Explain unloaded models show state UNAVAILABLE reason 'unloaded' in the index
cases.ground_truth: Explicit mode exposes `/v2/repository/models/<model>/load` and `/unload`. Returns HTTP 200.

cases.prompt: I want Triton to automatically pick up changes to my model repository without restarting.
expected_behavior: Start tritonserver with `--model-control-mode=poll --repository-poll-secs=<N>`
Explain that file or config.pbtxt edits are picked up at the next poll
Note the server logs 'loading' / 'successfully loaded' / 'successfully unloaded <old>' lines
cases.ground_truth: Poll mode reloads models on next poll after a file change; log shows load + unload of the old version.

cases.prompt: Triton says `Internal: failed to stat file /models/mymodel/1/model.onnx` but my file is right there. What's wrong?
expected_behavior: Check the actual filename inside 1/
Diagnose: the file is not named exactly `model.onnx`
Offer two fixes: rename to model.onnx, or set `default_model_filename` in config.pbtxt
cases.ground_truth: `failed to stat file ... model.onnx` always means the file is named something else. Fix by rename or default_model_filename.

cases.prompt: My ONNX model doesn't show up in /v2/repository/index at all. Not even UNAVAILABLE. What happened?
expected_behavior: Check the server log for `Error parsing text-format inference.ModelConfig`
Diagnose: config.pbtxt has an invalid value (common: `data_type: float32` instead of TYPE_FP32)
Fix by using the correct TYPE_* enum spelling
cases.ground_truth: A protobuf parse failure makes the model invisible from the index; only the log shows the cause.

cases.prompt: I put my ONNX file under v1/ but Triton refuses to load my model. There's no error in the index.
expected_behavior: Check the server log for `ignore version directory 'v1' which fails to convert to integral number`
Diagnose: version directories must be integers like 1/, 2/, 3/
Fix by renaming v1/ to 1/
cases.ground_truth: Non-integer version directories are ignored; model drops out of the index with a warning in the log.

cases.prompt: Triton reports `Invalid argument: unexpected inference input 'X', allowed inputs are: INPUT0, INPUT1`. Why?
expected_behavior: Diagnose: the input name in config.pbtxt does not match the ONNX graph
Point at the allowed names in the error
Fix by renaming the input in config.pbtxt, or inspecting the ONNX graph for the real names
cases.ground_truth: `unexpected inference input` means the config name differs from the ONNX graph. The error lists the real names.

cases.prompt: I'm getting `Invalid argument: unexpected inference output 'WRONG_OUT', allowed outputs are: OUTPUT0`. How do I fix the config?
expected_behavior: Diagnose: output name mismatch between config.pbtxt and the ONNX graph
Fix by renaming the output to one of the allowed names
cases.ground_truth: Same pattern as input mismatch. The error lists valid output names.

cases.prompt: My Python client is sending a tensor with shape [4] but Triton rejects it saying `Expected [-1,4], got [4]. NOTE: Setting a non-zero max_batch_size in the model config requires a non-trivial batch dim`. The model config says max_batch_size 4.
expected_behavior: Diagnose: max_batch_size > 0 requires the request to include a batch dim
Fix by sending shape [1, 4] instead of [4]
Or set max_batch_size: 0 in config.pbtxt if batching is not wanted
cases.ground_truth: When max_batch_size>0, the wire shape must include the batch dim; the server prepends [-1,...] to the config dims.

cases.prompt: Client gets HTTP 404 `Request for unknown model: 'mymodel' has no available versions` but the model directory exists.
expected_behavior: Check /v2/repository/index for the model's state
If UNAVAILABLE, read the reason and fix the load error
Confirm the model is READY before retrying the inference call
cases.ground_truth: `no available versions` means the model failed to load. Diagnosis starts at the repository index.

cases.prompt: I'm trying to call version 2 of my model but the client gets `Request for unknown model: 'mymodel' version 2 is not found`.
expected_behavior: Check version_policy in config.pbtxt
Add version 2 to the policy (or switch to `all: {}`) if it should be served
Or call a version the policy includes
cases.ground_truth: A version excluded by policy returns HTTP 404 `version X is not found`. Fix by adjusting version_policy.

cases.prompt: My client calls `is_server_ready()` and gets False, but other models are serving fine. What does ready mean here?
expected_behavior: Explain server ready is strict: True only when every model is READY
Use `is_server_live()` for process liveness
Use `is_model_ready("<model>")` for per-model routing decisions
cases.ground_truth: `is_server_ready()` is a catalog-level boolean; one failed model makes it False even if others serve correctly.

cases.prompt: Write me a Python client that calls my Triton ONNX model over HTTP.
expected_behavior: Use tritonclient.http.InferenceServerClient('host:8000')
Create InferInput per model input with the correct name, shape, and FP32-style datatype
Call client.infer(model_name, inputs) and read result.as_numpy('<output>')
cases.ground_truth: Standard tritonclient.http recipe: InferenceServerClient → InferInput → infer → as_numpy.

cases.prompt: Same inference but over gRPC for lower latency.
expected_behavior: Swap tritonclient.http for tritonclient.grpc
Change port 8000 to 8001
Rest of the code pattern is identical
cases.ground_truth: tritonclient.grpc is a drop-in replacement; port 8001; same API.

cases.prompt: Can I call my Triton model from curl without a Python client?
expected_behavior: Use `POST /v2/models/<model>/infer` with JSON body
Body includes `inputs: [{name, shape, datatype, data}]` and `outputs`
Note binary tensor headers (Inference-Header-Content-Length) for large tensors
cases.ground_truth: REST inference via `POST /v2/models/<model>/infer` with KFServing v2 JSON body.

cases.prompt: My Python client passes 'TYPE_FP32' as the datatype and gets an error. What datatype string does InferInput want?
expected_behavior: Explain the three different spellings: TYPE_FP32 in config.pbtxt, "FP32" in InferInput, np.float32 in numpy
Point at references/datatypes.md for the full table
cases.ground_truth: config uses `TYPE_FP32`, client uses `"FP32"`, numpy uses `np.float32`. Three spellings, one dtype.

cases.prompt: I have a model.pt TorchScript file. Help me serve it on Triton.
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a PyTorch skill case
If the catalog has triton-pytorch-model-repository, route there
cases.ground_truth: This is out of scope for triton-onnx-model-repository. .pt requires a sibling skill.

cases.prompt: Deploy my resnet.plan TensorRT engine on Triton.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Route to triton-tensorrt-model-repository if present
cases.ground_truth: TensorRT engines (.plan) are covered by a separate Triton TRT skill.

cases.prompt: Create a Kubernetes Deployment YAML for Triton serving my ONNX model with 3 replicas and a Service.
expected_behavior: Stay silent; Kubernetes orchestration is out of scope
Suggest the Triton Kubernetes deployment skill (separate)
cases.ground_truth: Kubernetes deployment is a different skill. This skill only covers docker-run and tritonserver direct invocation.

cases.prompt: I want to chain an ONNX preprocessing model and an ONNX inference model into a Triton ensemble.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Point at a Triton ensemble skill (when it exists)
cases.ground_truth: Ensembles are out of scope per Limitations.

cases.prompt: Deploy NVIDIA Dynamo on my Kubernetes cluster with disaggregated workers.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Route to dynamo-recipe-runner
cases.ground_truth: Dynamo is a different product and has its own skill family.

cases.prompt: Solve a vehicle routing problem with cuOpt.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Route to the cuOpt skill if present
cases.ground_truth: cuOpt is unrelated to Triton ONNX serving.

cases.prompt: How do I iterate over a dictionary in Python?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a general Python question, no ONNX, no Triton
cases.ground_truth: Nothing in this prompt invokes the skill's trigger conditions.

cases.prompt: Train an ONNX model from scratch with PyTorch.
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this skill is about inference serving, not training
cases.ground_truth: Training is out of scope. The skill starts from a trained .onnx file.

cases.prompt: Run inference on my ONNX model using the ONNX Runtime Python package directly, not Triton.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Suggest the user use `onnxruntime` Python package directly, outside this skill's scope
cases.ground_truth: ONNX Runtime standalone is not Triton. This skill only covers Triton serving.

cases.prompt: Deploy my ONNX model on AWS SageMaker.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
This is not Triton deployment
cases.ground_truth: SageMaker is a different serving platform; out of scope.

cases.prompt: Set up TLS and authentication for my Triton server so only authorized clients can call it.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Note this skill is dev setup only; production security is a separate concern
cases.ground_truth: TLS and auth are out of scope per Limitations.

cases.prompt: Use the Triton Model Orchestrator to run BLS logic on my requests.
expected_behavior: Stay silent
Model orchestrator and BLS are out of scope
cases.ground_truth: Business Logic Scripting and the Triton Model Orchestrator are not covered here.

cases.prompt: What's the difference between ONNX and TorchScript as model formats?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a comparison question, not a Triton deployment task
The prompt mentions ONNX but does not ask to serve, deploy, or run a model
cases.ground_truth: Mere mention of ONNX is not sufficient to trigger. The skill requires a serving, deployment, config, or debugging intent.

cases.prompt: How do I export my PyTorch model to ONNX format?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a conversion question, not a Triton serving task
No Triton or model-repository intent in the prompt
cases.ground_truth: Conversion from PyTorch to ONNX is a pre-step. This skill starts from an existing .onnx file.

cases.prompt: My ONNX model throws an opset version error when I load it with onnxruntime.InferenceSession. How do I downgrade the opset?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is an ONNX Runtime standalone issue, not a Triton serving issue
No mention of Triton, config.pbtxt, or model repository
cases.ground_truth: ONNX Runtime standalone errors are out of scope. This skill is Triton-specific.

cases.prompt: Can you optimize my ONNX model for faster inference using quantization?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; model optimization and quantization are not in this skill's scope
Suggest an ONNX optimization skill if one exists
cases.ground_truth: Optimization and quantization live in separate skills. This one deploys an existing .onnx as-is.

cases.prompt: Why does my ONNX model give different outputs than the original PyTorch model I exported it from?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a numerical correctness / conversion debugging question
Not a Triton deployment issue
cases.ground_truth: Numerical differences from the source model are a conversion issue, out of scope.

cases.prompt: What tool can I use to visualize the graph of my ONNX model?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; visualization tools (Netron etc.) are not this skill's job
cases.ground_truth: Visualization is unrelated to Triton deployment.

cases.prompt: I have a trained model file and I want to set up a model repository so my service can call it. The file ends in .onnx.
expected_behavior: Infer that 'model repository' plus '.onnx' points at Triton ONNX serving
Run the usual 7-step recipe
Return the Output Contract
cases.ground_truth: The skill must fire even when the user does not explicitly say 'Triton'. 'model repository' + '.onnx' is enough context.

cases.prompt: model.onnx shows UNAVAILABLE in /v2/repository/index with reason 'failed to stat file'. What now?
expected_behavior: Recognize this as a Triton ONNX load failure
Diagnose as the wrong-filename case
Point at the fix in references/errors.md
cases.ground_truth: A pure error-string prompt with no 'Triton' keyword still triggers because of /v2/repository/index + .onnx.

cases.prompt: Can you write me a config.pbtxt for an ONNX classifier with 10 output classes and class labels?
expected_behavior: Recognize config.pbtxt + ONNX classifier + class labels as a label_filename case
Produce the config using references/config-pbtxt.md
Instruct the user on the labels.txt file placement
cases.ground_truth: `config.pbtxt` is a Triton concept; combined with ONNX, this must fire.

cases.prompt: Why does Triton reject my model with 'unexpected inference input'?
expected_behavior: Recognize the Triton error
Diagnose the input-name mismatch case from references/errors.md
Offer the fix
cases.ground_truth: A Triton error message is a trigger even without the user saying 'ONNX'; the agent should read the graph in Step 2 to recover names.

cases.prompt: I want to deploy my ResNet50 ONNX classifier to serve 1000 requests per second.
expected_behavior: Recognize 'deploy', 'ONNX', 'classifier' as positive triggers
Choose GPU target and dynamic batching defaults
Produce the Output Contract
cases.ground_truth: Product-name-level prompts with ONNX and deploy intent trigger normally.

cases.prompt: I just downloaded this ONNX file from HuggingFace. How do I get it running so my code can call it?
expected_behavior: Recognize this as the minimum-viable serving case
Default target to auto-detected GPU or CPU
Run auto-complete, no config.pbtxt
cases.ground_truth: The phrase 'running so my code can call it' is a serving intent even without 'Triton' keyword.

cases.prompt: I have an ONNX model but I want to convert it to TensorRT and then serve it on Triton.
expected_behavior: Stay silent; the user's end state is TensorRT serving, not ONNX serving
Route to the ONNX-to-TRT conversion skill, then triton-tensorrt-model-repository
cases.ground_truth: Final serving format decides the skill. If the user wants TRT serving, this skill should not fire.

cases.prompt: Help me serve my .pb TensorFlow model on Triton Inference Server.
expected_behavior: Stay silent; .pb is TensorFlow, routes to a Triton TensorFlow skill
Do not apply the ONNX recipe
cases.ground_truth: Triton serving is generic; this skill is ONNX-specific. Other backend files need their own skill.

cases.prompt: What is Triton Inference Server and what does it do?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a generic product overview question
No model file, no deployment intent
cases.ground_truth: This skill is a hands-on recipe. Overview answers come from docs, not the skill.

cases.prompt: Should I use TensorRT-LLM or Triton to serve my Llama ONNX export?
expected_behavior: Stay silent; this is a product-choice question, not a deployment task
LLM serving specifically has dedicated skills
cases.ground_truth: LLM serving (Llama, etc.) is explicitly out of scope per this skill's description.

cases.prompt: My Triton startup log says `Could not determine backend for model 'mymodel' with no backend in model configuration. Expected model name of the form 'model.<backend_name>'`. What am I missing?
expected_behavior: Diagnose: the version directory is empty or has no file, AND no `backend:` is set in config.pbtxt
Offer two fixes: place `model.onnx` in the version directory, or add `backend: "onnxruntime"` to config.pbtxt
Point at references/errors.md for the full entry
cases.ground_truth: `Could not determine backend` means the version directory is empty or has no recognizable file. Fix by placing model.onnx or setting backend: in config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: Triton logged `autofilled max_batch_size to 4 for model 'mymodel' since batching is supported but no max_batch_size is specified in model configuration`. Is this an error?
expected_behavior: Explain this is INFORMATIONAL, not an error
The server used the default of 4 because the ONNX graph has a dynamic axis and the config did not specify
To change: set `max_batch_size` explicitly in config.pbtxt, or pass `--backend-config=default-max-batch-size=<N>` at startup
cases.ground_truth: The autofilled warning is informational. Fix only if 4 is wrong for the use case.

cases.prompt: How can I tell from the Triton metrics whether dynamic batching is actually coalescing my requests?
expected_behavior: Scrape `/metrics` on port 8002
Compare `nv_inference_count` to `nv_inference_exec_count`
Ratio of count / exec_count is batcher efficiency; higher ratio means more coalescing
Point at references/metrics.md
cases.ground_truth: `nv_inference_count / nv_inference_exec_count` is the coalescing ratio. 1.0 means no batching happening; higher means the batcher is working.

cases.prompt: Why do some of my models show up in /v2/repository/index with a state of READY, some with UNAVAILABLE, some with just a name field, and some are missing entirely?
expected_behavior: Explain the four shapes: READY+version, UNAVAILABLE+reason, name-only, absent
Name-only means `config.pbtxt` failed to parse
Absent means the version directory was not an integer
Point at the index-shape list in Step 6 and references/errors.md
cases.ground_truth: `/v2/repository/index` returns four distinct entry shapes; each corresponds to a different failure or success state.

cases.prompt: What's the difference between /v2/health/live, /v2/health/ready, and /v2/models/<model>/ready?
expected_behavior: `/v2/health/live` means the server process is up; use for liveness probes
`/v2/health/ready` means every loaded model is READY; strict, False if any model failed
`/v2/models/<model>/ready` means that specific model is READY; use for routing decisions
Point at Step 6's health-endpoints table
cases.ground_truth: Three endpoints, three granularities: process, catalog, individual model. Server-ready is strict.

cases.prompt: I want you to show me the generated config.pbtxt for review before you start the Triton server.
expected_behavior: Set `review` to `true` (or keep the default)
After Step 4 writes config.pbtxt, print the full contents and pause for user confirmation
Proceed to Step 5 only after the user approves
cases.ground_truth: The `review` input gates a pause between Step 4 and Step 5 so the user can inspect the generated config.pbtxt.

cases.prompt: Don't actually run the Docker commands on my machine. Just give me the exact commands I need to run myself.
expected_behavior: Set `execute` to `false`
Still run Step 2 (inspect the ONNX graph read-only)
Produce the model repository layout as text, not on disk
Produce the server command literally but do not invoke Docker
Produce the client snippet without executing it
Return the Output Contract with 'Not executed' for the smoke-test result
cases.ground_truth: `execute: false` turns the skill into a command generator. Nothing mutates on the host; the Output Contract is complete minus the smoke-test result.

cases.prompt: Help me serve this .onnx model.
expected_behavior: Recognize the bare combination of `.onnx` and `serve` as sufficient trigger context
Ask for the path to the file if not supplied
Default all other inputs and run the recipe
cases.ground_truth: Minimal wording with `.onnx` and `serve` is still the skill's trigger. The agent should not hesitate.

cases.prompt: I'm serving this ONNX model on an A100. Can you make it faster?
expected_behavior: Set `accelerator` to `tensorrt`
Append the `optimization { execution_accelerators { gpu_execution_accelerator ... } }` block to config.pbtxt with name tensorrt, precision_mode FP16, max_workspace_size_bytes 1073741824
Enable `model_warmup` so the first-load compile does not block the first request
Expect about 2x throughput and halved latency per Triton docs
cases.ground_truth: ORT-TRT is the standard GPU performance path for ONNX on Triton. Published lift: ~2x throughput, ~50% latency. The compile step requires model_warmup to avoid first-request slowness.

cases.prompt: My ONNX model runs on Intel Xeon CPUs in production. Can I accelerate it without a GPU?
expected_behavior: Set `accelerator` to `openvino`
Append the `optimization { execution_accelerators { cpu_execution_accelerator: [{ name: "openvino" }] } }` block to config.pbtxt
Note openvino is Intel CPU only; non-Intel CPUs gain nothing or fail
cases.ground_truth: ORT-OpenVINO accelerates ONNX inference on Intel CPUs. Set only when the host is Intel; AMD or ARM CPUs get no benefit.

cases.prompt: Triton won't load my ONNX model. The log shows `[ONNXRuntimeError] : 9 : NOT_IMPLEMENTED : Could not find an implementation for <OpType>(<opset>) node with name 'X'`. What's the fix?
expected_behavior: Diagnose: ONNX graph uses an op at an opset version the bundled ONNX Runtime does not support
Fix: re-export the model at a lower supported opset. Safe range on recent Triton (verified 26.10: opset 23 still works for common ops)
Alternative: upgrade Triton to a container with a newer ORT
Note: the exact opset threshold depends on the Triton release
cases.ground_truth: `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with an opset number means that particular op at that opset is beyond the bundled ORT. Verified on Triton 26.10: opset 23 common ops still load. The failure threshold is version-dependent.

cases.prompt: ONNX model fails to load on CPU with `[ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : ... CustomOpX is not implemented for CPU`. The same model loads fine when I force GPU. What are my options?
expected_behavior: Diagnose: the ONNX op is GPU-only in the bundled ORT
Fix 1: set `instance_group: [{ kind: KIND_GPU }]` to route the model to GPU
Fix 2: re-export the ONNX without the unsupported op
Point at references/errors.md Unsupported operator on target device
cases.ground_truth: Op not implemented for the target device means the op exists in ORT only for the other device. Fix by switching instance_group or re-exporting.
